Transmission facilities include a 525-kV line from the proposed Bad Creek site to the Oconee Nuclear Station for transmitting plant output and a 100-kV line from the Jocassee switchyard to the proposed Bad Creek site to be used initially for construction power to Bad Creek. Rights-of-way widths vary over different sections of these lines. Table 3-1 and Figure 3-3, when used together, describe these rights-of-way (ROW), break them down into sections giving specifications for each, and show their relationship to the already existing transmission rights-of-way by means of a schematic drawing.
While the proposed transmission facilities and rightsof-way are not extensive by themselves, their addition to an existing system would be significant. Impacts would result from the placement of the proposed transmission lines due to the visual intrusion of 7.67 miles of new 254-foot ROW (Table 3-1, Section A) and 1.04 miles of new 200-foot ROW (Table 3-1, Section E). About 11 miles of ROW ranging from 50 to 175 feet wide (Table 3-1, Sections C, D, and F), as an addition to an existing 270-foot ROW, would be intrusive because of its path across topography that has little variation in the continuity of vegetative density (dense) and slope (moderate to generally steep). There weld be little likelihood of repeated or prolonged views of t o two lines on the new 254-foot ROW (Table 3-1, Section A), and therefore the impact would be moderate. On the other hand, although 10.92 miles of new line would require only from 50 to 175 feet of additional ROW (Table 3-1, Sections C, D, and F), the impacts would be a great deal more intrusive because: (1) construction of towers and the additional clearing necessary would disrupt an existing ROW (Table 3-1, Section B) that is almost void of any substantial vegetation that could facilitate a feathering technique along the edges of the ROW; (2) the 100-kV line (Table 3-1, Section F) would cross two arms of Lake Keowee and substantially affect another; (3) the 525kV line (Table 3-1, Sections C and D) would cross Lake Keowee five times and create substantial visual effects on the lake at three other locations; (4) the 525 kV-line would also cross a major highway once (SC 11) (Table 3-1, Section
